function: Learned setting of a tunable liquid lens at the MIMO VLC receiver (focal length, tilt angles) to focus LED light onto separate PDs and minimize BER (pp. 3, 8).
system: Indoor MIMO VLC with GSM: 16 or 36 ceiling LEDs, 16 to 64 PDs behind a tunable liquid convex lens; no RIS; visible light (pp. 3-4, 10, 13).
method: Blockwise CNN (position and orientation estimation), LSTM/BiLSTM (prediction), and dense regression (lens parameters); supervised block-wise training, MSE loss, SGD, labels from exhaustive search (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Lambertian LoS gain times geometric-optics lens imaging gain, clothoid mobility, AR orientation model of [26]; 10^7 simulated realizations for training and testing (pp. 4-6, 11).
test_conditions: One simulated set split 70/10/20% for training, validation, testing; results varied over SNR, orientation variance, NI, Nr, Nt, LED/PD spacing, GSM/SM/SMP; retraining per condition unstated (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Non-learned only: exhaustive search, VULO fixed lens, CLS closed-form scheme, no lens adjustment, upward receiver, LC-based IRS receiver of [16]; no learned baseline (pp. 7, 10, 12).
metrics: BER versus average SNR, orientation variance, and inter-LED distance; MSE of position and orientation prediction versus window size; average ML execution time (pp. 11-13).
complexity: Multiplication and summation counts per PBML block, Eqs. (34)-(39) (p. 9); average ML execution time 9.4 ms on a laptop CPU/GPU (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "Lambertian model is used to obtain"; p. 11: "channel realizations were generated". Custom simulator (Lambertian LoS plus geometric lens optics); no standardized channel model or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "training, validation, and testing and were selected as 70%, 10%, and 20%"; p. 9: "valid for a given LED placement and receiver architecture". Held-out split only; no stated test of the trained model in unseen conditions.
q3_support: p. 7: "compare their performance with two baseline schemes, namely vertical upward lens orientation (VULO) and exhaustive search"; p. 12: "compare our schemes with the liquid crystal (LC)-based IRS receiver". No learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 9: "the number of calculations involved in each block in terms of multiplication operations and summation operations are presented"; p. 11: "The average execution time for the ML architecture was found to be 9.4 ms".
q5_support: p. 11: "The evaluation was performed by MATLAB and Python"; data are simulated, and the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Page 1 holds the title 'Liquid Lens-Based Imaging Receiver for MIMO VLC Systems' and DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2025.3588562. Inclusion and area are a judgment for the reviewer: the learned PBML outputs the focal length and tilt angles of a liquid lens at the VLC receiver (p. 8: "The output layer consists of 3 nodes to obtain optimal"), which steer and focus the received light beams (p. 2: "focus light beams coming from LEDs on to separated PDs"), so I mapped it to area 3 (beams of a reconfigurable element, compared with an LC-based IRS receiver on p. 12). The lens is neither a base station precoder nor an RIS, so the reviewer may instead judge it outside the seven areas (function). Position estimation (CNN) and prediction (LSTM) are internal blocks; the output is the lens setting and the main metric is BER. The link is optical (visible light), not RF; Step 1 has no band criterion. ris = 0 because the lens is refractive; the LC-based IRS receiver of [16] is only a comparison. q1: the orientation model of [26] derives from measurements but only parameterizes the simulator. q2: Figs. 8-10 vary the MIMO scheme, orientation variance, Nt, Nr, and spacing without saying whether PBML was retrained. q3: CLS is the authors' own non-learned scheme, and exhaustive search also produced the training labels (p. 9).
